Moon Trades S.R.L. is a Romanian deep-tech micro-enterprise dedicated to lunar In-Situ Resource Utilisation (ISRU), regolith intelligence, and autonomous robotics for planetary exploration. Headquartered in Iași, Romania, Moon Trades develops foundational technologies that bridge terrestrial mining heritage and the emerging space resources economy.
Core focus areas:- Lunar geotechnical characterisation and core sampling — addressing the foundational measurement gap in current ISRU roadmaps, drawing on three generations of terrestrial mining and engineering heritage.- Real-time multi-spectral mineral analysis through the company's flagship technology platform (A.P.E.X. — Apollo-Powered Exploration eXpedition), enabling in-situ assessment of lunar regolith composition during exploration and mining operations.- Autonomous robotics and soil intelligence systems designed for the lunar surface and post-gravity operational environments.- Systems-architecture services for partners building lunar infrastructure, ISRU pilot plants, and the broader Mearth (Moon-Earth) economy.
Moon Trades operates under the principle of design with discipline — engineering rigour combined with ethical, human-centred, and decentralised system thinking. The company actively seeks collaboration with ESA programmes, European primes, research institutions, and SMEs working on Terrae Novae, PROSPECT, Moonlight, lunar lander payloads, ISRU demonstrators, and related initiatives.

entityDescription:
The Montagne Fiorentine Model Forest Association (FMMF) it was the first Model Forest established in Italy and is located in Tuscany, in the eastern area of the Metropolitan City of Florence. Covering around 548 km² and involving seven municipalities, FMMF is a non-profit, voluntary association that promotes sustainable forest and rural landscape management through an inclusive, participatory governance approach.
FMMF brings together public institutions, private companies, local communities, researchers and civil society to enhance the environmental, social and economic value of forest ecosystems. Its activities focus on sustainable wood supply chains, biodiversity conservation, local development, eco-tourism, environmental education and innovation in rural areas. The association aims to strengthen cooperation among stakeholders and improve the resilience of forest territories.
Model Forests (MFs) are internationally recognized governance platforms that originated in Canada in the early 1990s. They are based on multi-stakeholder partnerships working together to balance forest conservation, sustainable resource use and community development at landscape scale.
FMMF is part of the International Model Forest Network (IMFN), the largest global network dedicated to sustainable landscape governance, connecting more than 60 Model Forests worldwide. It also plays an active role in the Mediterranean Model Forest Network Secretariat (MMFNs) managed by Tuscany Region, fostering collaboration, knowledge exchange and joint actions among territories facing similar ecological and socio-economic challenges across the Mediterranean region.

entityDescription: A significant development for the public health sector of Cyprus is the official establishment of the Cyprus International Institute for Environmental and Public Health (CII / Institute) as a Public Health Research Unit. The Institute is now officially part of the School of Health Sciences of the Cyprus University of Technology (CUT), by decision of the House of Representatives, as published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Cyprus, on 20 June 2025 (G.O.P. 174/2025).The Cyprus International Institute for Environmental and Public Health is the longest-standing scientific entity in Cyprus that focuses exclusively on the study of the impact of environmental factors on public health. The Institute offers specialized educational and research programs, while over time it has substantially contributed to society through initiatives, epidemiological studies and interventions on key issues related to environmental and public health, with particular emphasis on chronic disease prevention and control, including health promotion and education. The institutionalization of the Institute strengthens its development and sustainability, promotes extroversion for the expansion of its international collaborations in the Eastern Mediterranean and Europe, making it the strategic pillar of public health in the region, and beyond.The Institute was established in 2004, based on the agreement between the Republic of Cyprus and the Harvard School of Public Health. In 2009, the Institute was integrated into the Cyprus University of Technology, based on a tripartite agreement with the Harvard School of Public Health and the Republic of Cyprus. After the end of the official collaboration with HSPH in 2016, it continued its upward trajectory within the School of Health Sciences at CUT, utilizing the know-how and experience acquired through the valuable transatlantic collaboration with Harvard University.Since its establishment, the Institute has established itself as one of the most reputable academic and research institutions in the field of Environmental and Public Health in the Republic of Cyprus. With a presence spanning over two decades, it consistently offers successful postgraduate and doctoral programs, conducts important population-based public health studies, and produces scientific data with substantial social impact. It has created an international network of more than 200 alumni –Cypriot and international – who excel in Europe, America, Asia, and Africa, contributing to the visibility of Cyprus on a global level. During the last ten consecutive years, it has been annually organizing the Pancyprian Public Health Conference, offering an open platform for information and communication on health issues between scientists, policymakers and civil society.In the post-pandemic era, where public health is at the top of the priorities of both the European Union and the Republic of Cyprus, the role of the Institute becomes even more crucial. The systematic production and utilization of scientific data for monitoring the health of the population is a cornerstone for the development of effective and sustainable health policies. Public health is not limited to the provision of services, but extends to the prevention, early diagnosis and control of diseases. Modern, smart health systems must be based on the principles and best practices of public health, in order to ensure social cohesion and the quality of life of citizens.

Larnaka Municipality is a modern and dynamic local authority that keeps pace with emerging trends and addresses the challenges of contemporary society. The Municipality has extensive experience in the development and implementation of projects aimed at enhancing the urban environment of Larnaka and has actively participated in several EU-funded networks and programmes. Furthermore, the Municipal Department of Technical Services, Planning and Works is currently developing a number of projects with strong potential to attract European Union funding. The Municipality employs approximately 400 staff members across its various departments and services.
Following the Local Government Reform implemented in Cyprus on 1 July 2024, the Municipality of Larnaka was administratively restructured through its merger with the former local authorities of Livadia and Voroklini (Oroklini). The newly established municipality covers an area of approximately 56.95 km², comprising Larnaka (32.9 km²), Livadia (8.65 km²) and Voroklini (15.4 km²).

• Livadia: 8,581 inhabitants, DEGURBA 1, LAU Code 4011
• Voroklini (Oroklini): 7,575 inhabitants, DEGURBA 2, LAU Code 4102
Accordingly, the total population of the newly established Municipality of Larnaka amounts to 68,194 inhabitants, serving an area of approximately 56.95 km². The Municipality plays a key role in promoting sustainable urban development, environmental protection, social inclusion and economic growth, while supporting the broader strategic vision of Larnaka as a resilient, innovative and attractive Mediterranean city.

Thales Digital Solutions Inc. leverage the experience and expertise accrued from many other country business units and supporting suppliers. With more than 100 employees across two offices located in the province of Quebec, it has proven expertise, capability, and experience in the design, delivery, and support of best-in-breed digital technologies.
AI is a cornerstone of Thales Digital Solutions’ strategy to drive digital transformation for its clients across multiple domains. The cortAIx platform centralizes AI innovation, making it a reusable and scalable resource that enriches Thales’ portfolio of services and products. By embedding AI technologies into their digital solutions, Thales enhances capabilities such as real-time decision support, predictive maintenance, cybersecurity threat detection, identity verification, and autonomous systems operation. The AI capabilities developed through cortAIx help deliver smarter, more agile, and more secure technologies that meet the evolving needs of governments and industries worldwide. Thales cortAIx – with its Labs and Factory components – is a key enabler within Thales Digital Solutions, facilitating the end-to-end journey from AI research and innovation to production-ready intelligent systems, ensuring that AI becomes a strategic advantage in delivering value-added digital services.
cortAIx is Thales’ advanced AI-powered platform designed to accelerate the development and deployment of innovative digital solutions. It acts as a comprehensive ecosystem combining AI capabilities with the company’s expertise in security, data, and systems engineering. The cortAIx platform is structured around two main components: (1) cortAIx Labs representing the innovation and research arm of the platform where AI models, algorithms, and pilot projects are developed and experimented with. cortAIx Labs focuses on leveraging cutting-edge AI techniques – including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and advanced analytics – to create proof-of-concept solutions addressing real-world challenges. It serves as a creative environment for multidisciplinary teams to collaborate and rapidly explore new AI-driven ideas, particularly tailored to sectors like defense, aerospace, cybersecurity, transportation, and identity management. (2) cortAIx Factory: Once AI solutions are validated in the Labs, they transition into the cortAIx Factory, which is dedicated to scaling, industrializing, and operationalizing those AI models. The Factory ensures that AI applications are robust, secure, compliant, and efficiently integrated into Thales’ broader digital ecosystem and customer infrastructures. It also supports continuous monitoring, maintenance, and lifecycle management of AI models in production environments, facilitating smooth deployment at scale.
With more than 25 scientists (with MSc, PhD, or postdoc), Thales Digital Solutions’ senior scientists are not only coaching internally but also acting as research collaborators with our academic partners and government agencies and co-supervise MSc and PhD students through NSERC and MITACS research agreements. Thales Digital Solutions’ senior scientists are also affiliated to academic partners as associate professors, regularly contributing as jury members/evaluators for master and PhD theses. They are also peer-reviewing journal papers and conference articles, are editorial board members for journals, are members of national and international scientific workgroups and participate in organizing international conferences.

entityName: UNIMORE - Artificial Intelligence Research and Innovation Center (AIRI)
entityDescription:
Artificial Intelligence Research and Innovation Center is University of Modena and Reggio Emilia’s Research Centre focused on ICT technologies and, in particular, Artificial Intelligence. It was promoted by the “Enzo Ferrari” Department of Engineering and the “Marco Biagi” Department of Economics of the University of Modena and Reggio Emilia. Recently, the Department of Physical, Computer and Mathematical Sciences and the Department of Sciences and Methods for Engineering have also become part of AIRI. AIRI is an accredited laboratory of the Emilia-Romagna Region High Technology Network and one of the leading laboratories of the Modena Technopole.
AIRI promotes, coordinates and carries out applied research, industrial research and technology transfer activities in the ICT sector, with particular reference to technologies based on Artificial Intelligence, including Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing and cognitive robotics, as well as Bioinformatics and Big Data. It also works on the related organizational and business models, positioning itself as a reference partner for companies that produce or use advanced ICT tools, and for public bodies wishing to support the innovation and competitiveness of such companies.
To this end, the Centre provides consultancy and applied research services for companies that produce or use ICT solutions and intelligent services; participates in technological research and development projects at regional, national, European and international levels; collaborates with regional, national, European and international public and private organizations; organizes conferences and specialized seminars; and carries out training activities for companies.
Over the last three years, AIRI has developed public and private research projects in Artificial Intelligence and related and complementary disciplines, mainly oriented towards Augmented Intelligence: systems and services for people, aimed at improving the cognitive capabilities of workers, citizens and individuals from a Human-Centric AI perspective. Examples include services for medicine, cultural heritage, intelligent maintenance, worker safety, anomaly analysis and citizen safety.
AIRI has participated in several national clusters and is actively involved in numerous national and international research projects on AI applied to computer vision and multimodal data analysis.
Over the last three years AIRI has been involved in more than 20 research projects with companies on AI topics related to industrial processes.
